q: Is induction hardening lower carbon than furnace hardening?
title: Induction vs furnace hardening
short: Often, for parts that need only a hard surface. Induction heats a thin surface layer with electricity in seconds, while a gas furnace heats the whole part and the furnace. The answer depends on your grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh) and the gas saved, so compare per part.

ul: Only the surface that needs hardening is heated.
No furnace to keep hot between batches.
Short cycle, so little standing loss.
Case carburising, which needs time at temperature in a controlled atmosphere.

p: Induction: kWh per part (from a sub-meter) multiplied by 0.710. Furnace: gas per batch multiplied by 2.05 kg CO2 per scm, divided by parts per batch, plus any endothermic gas used.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
